Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Captures unmeasured lake specific differences in water chemistry, productivity, and catchment characteristics.

Description...Unit: Index based on % cover of bedrock, boulders, cobble, gravel, sand, mud, and organic matter
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Important for burrowing and shelter availability. Coarser substrates increase shelter availability through more crevices.

Description...Unit: Slope from shoreline to the 5 m depth contour
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Steeper slopes facilitate access to deeper water during daylight refuging and associate with coarser substrates.

Description...Unit: Percentage cover of vegetation growing in the riparian zone
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Contributes detrital inputs, bank stability, and shading at the water’s edge.

Description...Unit: Percentage cover of trees hanging over the shoreline
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Provides direct shading and structural inputs into littoral habitats.
References: Smith et al., (1996); Vedia et al., (2017)

Description...Unit: Cover of wooden logs and tree branches in the sample site
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Provides physical structure creating refuge spaces and supports macroinvertebrate prey availability.

Description...Unit: Percentage cover of vegetation divided over emergent/submerged and native/non-native species
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Native vegetation provides cover and food source; non-native may alter movement and habitat conditions.
Influences metabolic rate, activity, physiological stress, and habitat suitability.
References: Devcich, (1979); Hammond et al., (2006); Parkyn et al., (2002); Parkyn & Collier, (2002); Angilletta et al., (2004)

Description...Unit: Dissolved oxygen concentration in mg L⁻¹
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Essential for respiration; reduced oxygen may constrain activity and habitat use.
References: Hammond et al., (2006); Broughton et al., (2017)

Description...Unit: Electrical conductivity of the water in µS cm⁻¹
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Reflects overall lake productivity, supporting food availability.

Description...Unit: Acidity or alkalinity of the water
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Influences moulting success and exoskeleton strength, affected by acidity or calcium levels.

Description...Unit: Presence/absence of selected native and non-native fish species
Hypothesised.importance.for.kōura: Fish act as predators, competitors, or indirectly modify habitat structure.
References: Shave et al., (1994); Barnes, (1996); Usio & Townsend, (2000); Barnes & Hicks, (2003)
